events.title: Rahab's Scarlet Cord
events.subtitle: A single thread of faith hanging from a window in the wall
story: Two spies, sent secretly from Shittim, slipped into Jericho, the city of palms. The place they came to was the house of a woman named Rahab, built into the city wall. But word travelled fast. Soon it reached the king that men of Israel had come to spy out the land. At sunset the king's men knocked at her door. Bring out the men who came into your house.

Rahab had already taken the two up to the roof and hidden them under the stalks of flax laid out to dry. Rahab said, the men left around the time the gate was shut. Hurry after them and you will catch them. The pursuers ran off toward the fords of the Jordan, and the city gate was shut. That night Rahab came up to the roof and said, we have heard how the Lord dried up the water of the Red Sea before you. When we heard it, our hearts melted.

Rahab let them down by a rope through her window, outside the city wall. The spies made her a promise. When we come into this land, tie this scarlet cord in the window you let us down through. And gather your father and mother, your brothers and all your family into your house. The two hid in the hills for three days, then crossed the river and went back to Joshua and reported. The Lord has truly given the whole land into our hands.

words.text: The Lord your God is God in heaven above and on the earth below.
I have shown you kindness, so swear to me by the Lord. Show kindness to my father's household too, and save our lives from death.
Our lives for yours. When the Lord gives us this land, we will deal faithfully with you.

events.note: Jericho is an oasis city in the Jordan Valley about 250 metres below sea level, counted among the oldest towns in the world. The flax drying on the roof recalls the spring harvest season. Rahab's name also appears in the genealogy of Jesus in Matthew's Gospel.
events.reflect: If a woman who lived in the city wall found her name in the Messiah's family line through a single scarlet cord, am I filtering out in advance, by my own standards, the people God may use?

quiz.q: What did Rahab tie in her window as a sign that she would be saved?
quiz.explain: The spies told Rahab to tie a scarlet cord in the window through which she had let them down (Josh 2:18, 21).

events.title: Crossing the Jordan
events.subtitle: The waters stop, and stones become memory
story: It was the time of the spring harvest, and the Jordan had swollen over its banks. On the shore, beside the rushing muddy water, the people stayed three days, looking across to the other side. An order went round the camp. When the ark of the covenant moves, follow it, but do not come too close. Joshua said, Consecrate yourselves, for tomorrow the Lord will do wonders among you.

The next day the priests carrying the ark went ahead down to the water. The moment their feet dipped into the river, the water flowing down from upstream piled up like a dam far away beside the town of Adam and stood still. While the priests stood firm on dry ground in the middle of the river, all the people crossed over opposite Jericho. Only the sound of feet on pebbles filled the riverbed.

Twelve men, one chosen from each tribe, each hoisted a stone onto his shoulder from the middle of the river and carried it out. The stones were set up at Gilgal. They were a sign, so that one day, when children asked what these stones meant, they would be told of the day the waters of the Jordan were cut off. There the people were circumcised, and on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month they kept the Passover. The day after they ate the produce of the land, the manna that had fallen for forty years stopped.

words.text: Today I will begin to raise you up in the sight of all Israel, so that they will know that I am with you as I was with Moses.
Today I have rolled away from you the disgrace of Egypt.
When your children ask one day what these stones mean, tell them: Israel crossed this Jordan on dry ground.

events.note: The Jordan rises highest in spring, when the snows of Mount Hermon melt. The town of Adam is thought to be Tell ed Damiyeh, about 30 kilometres upstream, and there are records that during an earthquake in 1927 the banks nearby collapsed and blocked the river for a time. Views on the location of Gilgal differ.
events.reflect: The river stopped only after the priests' feet touched the water; do I wait to move until I see the whole way open, or do I take the first step into water that is still flowing?

quiz.q: After keeping the Passover at Gilgal and eating the produce of the land, what stopped the next day?
quiz.explain: The manna stopped the day after they ate the produce of the land, and from that year Israel ate the crops of Canaan (Josh 5:12).

events.title: The Walls Fall
events.subtitle: Seven days of silence before the shout
story: Afraid of the Israelites, Jericho had barred its gates tight. No one went in, and no one came out, and the morning sun shone on the empty walls. The Lord said to Joshua, See, I have handed Jericho over to you, with its king and its warriors. But the way the Lord showed him was not the sword. It was walking.

Once a day for six days, seven priests carrying rams' horn trumpets went around the city ahead of the ark, blowing the trumpets. The people did not say a word. All that could be heard was the trumpets and the tramp of feet. On the seventh day, at daybreak, they circled the city seven times. When the trumpets sounded a long blast, Joshua cried out. Shout, for the Lord has given you this city. All the people raised a great shout, and the walls collapsed where they stood.

Every life in the city was devoted to destruction, and the silver and gold, bronze and iron went into the Lord's treasury, the text records, briefly and heavily. Only the house where the scarlet cord hung was different. At Joshua's word the two spies went in and brought out Rahab, her father and mother, her brothers and all her family. The city burned, but Rahab lived, as had been promised, and from that day on she lived among Israel.

words.text: See, I have handed Jericho over to you, with its king and its warriors.
When the priests sound a long blast on the rams' horns and you hear it, have all the people give a great shout. Then the wall will collapse.
Shout! The Lord has given you the city.

events.note: Archaeologists disagree about Jericho's fallen walls. In the 1930s Garstang argued for a destruction around 1400 BC, Kenyon held that there was no walled city at that time, and later some scholars again supported the earlier date.
events.reflect: For six days, when nothing seemed to happen, they kept marching in silence; how long can I quietly keep up an obedience whose fruit I cannot yet see?

quiz.q: How many times did Israel march around Jericho on the seventh day?
quiz.explain: For six days they went around the city once a day, and on the seventh day they went around it seven times (Josh 6:3–4, 15).

events.title: Achan's Sin and the City of Ai
events.subtitle: When one hidden thing brings down a whole camp
story: The men who had gone to look over Ai, a small town east of Bethel, came back and said, There is no need to wear out the whole people. Two or three thousand men will be enough. So about three thousand went up. But they were driven back from the city gate and fled down the slope, and thirty-six of them fell. The people's hearts melted like water. Joshua tore his clothes, and with the elders, dust thrown on their heads, he lay face down before the ark until evening.

The Lord said, Get up. Israel has sinned. They have stolen what was devoted to me and hidden it among their own belongings. The next morning the lot narrowed from tribe to clan, from clan to household, then man by man, until at last it fell on Achan of the tribe of Judah. Achan hung his head and confessed. I saw a fine robe from Shinar, silver and a bar of gold, and I wanted them, and I took them. They are buried in the ground inside my tent.

Achan and everything that was his were taken to the Valley of Achor and stoned, and a great heap of stones was raised over them. After that the Lord said to Joshua, Do not be afraid. I have handed Ai over to you. Joshua drew the enemy out by pretending to flee before the city, and soldiers lying in ambush behind it rushed into the empty town and set it on fire. Ai became a heap of ruins, and so it remains to this day, the text says.

words.text: Get up. Why are you lying on your face like this? Israel has sinned. They have broken the covenant I commanded, stolen what was devoted to me and hidden it among their own belongings.
Do not be afraid or discouraged. Take the whole army and go up to Ai. I have handed over to you the king of Ai, his people, his city and his land.
It is true. I have sinned against the Lord, the God of Israel. I saw those things, I wanted them and I took them. They are buried in the ground inside my tent.

events.note: Ai means heap of ruins. It has traditionally been identified with et Tell, but that site turned out to be uninhabited in the Late Bronze Age, so some suggest other candidates such as Khirbet el Maqatir. The location is still debated.
events.reflect: What Achan hid was a cloak, some silver and a bar of gold, yet the whole camp was shaken; can I admit that a hidden sin I thought was only my own business is weighing on my community?

quiz.q: Where did Achan hide the things he had stolen?
options: In the ground inside his tent
quiz.explain: Achan confessed that the robe, the silver and the gold bar were hidden in the ground inside his tent (Josh 7:21–22).

events.title: Covenant Between Two Mountains
events.subtitle: Words heard by two mountains facing each other
story: The valley of Shechem is cut deep between two mountains. Mount Ebal stands to the north and Mount Gerizim to the south, facing each other. As Moses had commanded, Joshua built an altar on Mount Ebal of uncut stones that no iron tool had touched. On it the smoke of burnt offerings and peace offerings rose up.

Then, in the sight of the children of Israel, he copied the law of Moses onto those stones. The Levitical priests carrying the ark of the covenant stood in the middle, and the people lined up, half in front of Mount Gerizim and half in front of Mount Ebal. Elders, officials and judges were all there, and even the foreigners who lived among them.

Joshua opened the book of the law and began to read. The words of blessing and the words of curse crossed the valley, struck the slopes of the two mountains and echoed back. Of all that Moses had commanded, there was not a single word Joshua did not read. Women and children, and the foreigners living with them, heard every word that day.

words.text: If you build an altar of stones for me, do not build it with cut stones. If you use a tool on the stones, you defile it.
See, today I am setting before you a blessing and a curse. When you enter the land, proclaim the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
Of all that Moses had commanded, there was not a word that Joshua did not read before the whole assembly. The women, the children and the foreigners heard it too.

events.note: Shechem lies in the pass between Mount Ebal, about 940 metres high, and Mount Gerizim, a little over 880 metres. It is also where Abraham built his first altar in Canaan. Some regard a stone structure excavated on Mount Ebal in the 1980s as Joshua's altar, but the debate continues.
events.reflect: Blessing and curse echoed together between two mountains, and even women, children and foreigners heard every word; am I looking only toward the mountain that is easy to hear?

quiz.q: On which mountain did Joshua build the altar?
quiz.explain: Joshua built an altar to the Lord on Mount Ebal from stones no iron tool had touched (Josh 8:30–31).

events.title: Sun, Stand Still
events.subtitle: The day the Lord listened to one man's prayer
story: When he heard that Gibeon had made peace with Israel, Adoni Zedek king of Jerusalem was terrified. He sent word to the kings of Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish and Eglon. Come up and help me, and let us attack Gibeon. Soon the armies of the five kings surrounded Gibeon. The Gibeonites sent word urgently to Joshua at the camp in Gilgal. Do not abandon your servants. Come up quickly and save us.

The Lord said to Joshua, Do not be afraid of them, for I have handed them over to you. Joshua marched all night up the mountain road from Gilgal and fell on them at dawn. The Lord threw the enemy into confusion, and as they fled down the slope of Beth Horon, great hailstones poured down on them from the sky. More died from the hail than from the sword.

That day, in the sight of all Israel, Joshua spoke to the Lord. Sun, stand still over Gibeon. Moon, stop over the Valley of Aijalon. The sun stood in the middle of the sky and did not hurry to go down for almost a whole day. Never before or since has there been a day like it, when the Lord listened to a human voice like this. For the Lord fought for Israel.

words.text: Do not be afraid of them. I have handed them over to you; not one of them will be able to stand against you.
Sun, stand still over Gibeon. Moon, stop over the Valley of Aijalon.
Do not abandon your servants. Come up quickly, save us and help us.

events.note: Gibeon is el Jib, about nine kilometres northwest of Jerusalem, where jar handles inscribed with the name Gibeon and a large water pool have been excavated. As for the sun standing still, views differ: some take it as a literal miracle, others as poetic language quoted from the Book of Jashar.
events.reflect: The covenant with Gibeon was made through deception, yet Joshua climbed the mountain road all night to keep it; am I someone who keeps a promise to the end even when it has turned against me?

quiz.q: Where did Joshua tell the moon to stop?
quiz.explain: Joshua cried out, Sun, stand still over Gibeon, and moon, over the Valley of Aijalon (Josh 10:12).

events.title: Dividing the Land at Shiloh
events.subtitle: Writing the promise onto the map
story: Shiloh, a quiet hill in the hill country of Ephraim. The whole community of Israel gathered there and set up the tent of meeting. The days of fighting since they crossed the Jordan were behind them, and the land already lay subdued before them. Even so, seven tribes had still not received their share, and they only sat before their tents, hesitating.

Joshua called them and asked, How long will you put off going in to take the land the Lord, the God of your fathers, has given you? Choose three men from each tribe. Let them travel throughout the land, divide it into seven parts, and come back with a written record. But the Levites will have no share. The priesthood of the Lord is their inheritance.

The men set out, walking over hills and through valleys, writing down the name of every town, one by one, in a book. They brought the book back to the camp at Shiloh. Joshua cast lots before the Lord and gave the remaining tribes their land. At last the promise became land with names.

words.text: How long will you put off going to take possession of the land the Lord, the God of your ancestors, has given you?
Divide the land into seven parts, write them down and bring the description to me. I will cast lots for you here before the Lord our God.
The Levites will receive no share among you, because the priestly service of the Lord is their inheritance.

events.note: Shiloh is identified with Khirbet Seilun, about 30 kilometres north of Jerusalem. The tent of meeting remained there throughout the time of the judges, and the story of Eli and Hannah in 1 Samuel is also set at Shiloh. The exact spot where the tabernacle stood is unknown.
events.reflect: If the land had already been given and seven tribes still put off going to take it, am I putting off enjoying the grace God has already given me, with the excuse of “not yet”?

quiz.q: Into how many parts did Joshua have the remaining land divided and written down?
quiz.explain: For the seven tribes that had not yet received their inheritance, he had the land divided into seven parts and written down (Josh 18:2, 6, 9).

events.title: As for Me and My House
events.subtitle: The last question of an old leader
story: Many years later, Joshua called all the tribes of Israel together at Shechem. The elders and leaders, the judges and officials came and stood before God. Joshua told them the story that began in the house of Terah beyond the river. How God called Abraham, how he brought them out of Egypt, the road through the wilderness, and the day they crossed the Jordan.

Joshua passed on the word of the Lord just as the Lord had spoken it. I gave you a land you did not labour for, towns you did not build, vineyards and olive groves you did not plant. After he had passed on the Lord's words, Joshua looked around at the people. Now choose today whom you will serve. As for me and my house, we will serve the Lord. Even when he pressed them, saying they would not be able to serve the Lord, the people answered again and again. We too will serve the Lord.

That day Joshua made a covenant with the people and wrote it in the book of the law of God. He took a large stone and set it up under the oak beside the sanctuary. See, this stone will be our witness. It has heard every word the Lord has spoken. After that Joshua the servant of the Lord died at the age of a hundred and ten and was buried at Timnath Serah in the hill country of Ephraim. Israel served the Lord all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who outlived him.

words.text: I gave you a land you had not laboured for and towns you had not built. You live in them and eat the fruit of vineyards and olive groves you did not plant.
Choose for yourselves today whom you will serve. But as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.
We will serve the Lord our God and listen to his voice.

events.note: Shechem is Tell Balata near present-day Nablus, where Jacob once buried foreign idols under an oak. Scholars note that this covenant ceremony, moving from a review of history to demands, witnesses and a written record, resembles the form of ancient Near Eastern treaties.
events.reflect: Before pressing the people to decide, Joshua first declared his own household's choice; before I demand it of others, am I first showing whom my house serves?

quiz.q: How old was Joshua when he died?
quiz.explain: Joshua son of Nun died at the age of a hundred and ten and was buried at Timnath Serah (Josh 24:29–30). A hundred and twenty was Moses' age when he died.
